description: Baseline P0-P3 acceptance scan; existing migration snapshot ancestry check fails before implementation changes.

description: Reconciled order confirmation with ADR-0033 and repaired migration ancestry; process PostgreSQL tests exposed an accounting period date bug.

asi.learned: The production service uses Clock.Clock, and @effect/vitest supplies a test clock unless explicitly live; date-sensitive PostgreSQL tests must control/provide clock intentionally.

description: Align order confirmation with ADR-0033 and repair the migration snapshot ancestry chain.

asi.hypothesis: Server-derived order lines and accounting posting close the superseded workflow gap without broadening architecture.
asi.result: Process now reserves Sales-owned lines, derives revenue from order total, and no longer accepts client journal facts; tests and repository checks pass.
asi.test_clock_note: Date-sensitive @effect/vitest integration fixtures cover the epoch-based test clock explicitly.

description: Reconciled P0 and roadmap wording, but the current coarse metric already counted the conditional P0 readiness sentence.

description: Accept the P1 inventory primitive baseline and reconcile P0/roadmap status.

asi.hypothesis: A narrow discrete-stock baseline resolves P1 without speculative conversion, traceability, valuation, or location hierarchy.

asi.deferred: Implementation of UOM DTOs and idempotent correction command remains the next gate.

description: Implemented P1 UOM and correction semantics; one PostgreSQL assertion still queried the removed enum value.

asi.hypothesis: An idempotent signed adjustment command plus immutable item UOM closes the P1 implementation gate.
asi.rollback_reason: The integration test counted corrections with kind='adjustment' after implementation intentionally encoded correction direction as existing receipt/issue kinds to avoid unsafe same-transaction enum evolution.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply/retain the P1 patch and change the movement-count assertion to filter by correction idempotency key or non-null correction metadata, then rerun.
asi.migration_learning: Using existing receipt/issue direction plus correction metadata avoids PostgreSQL's unsafe-use-of-new-enum-value migration failure.

description: Implement immutable Item UOM and idempotent append-oriented stock corrections for the P1 baseline.

asi.result: Inventory now defaults/normalizes UOM, validates correction units, serializes negative corrections against reserved stock, and preserves correction history with tenant-scoped idempotency.
asi.validation: Inventory unit/PostgreSQL tests, migration catalog, db check, boundary lint, type check, and contract checks passed.
asi.migration_design: Corrections reuse receipt/issue movement direction plus correction metadata, avoiding a PostgreSQL enum migration transaction hazard.

description: Define and enforce the P2 document, fixed-scale money, revenue period, and reversal baseline.

description: Define the P3 boundary and add neutral typed catalog contracts with Inventory and Accounting contributors.

description: Complete the initial P0-P3 acceptance portfolio with explicit period-close concurrency evidence.

name: Add Sales order confirmation as the second Level 3 provider

description: Add Sales order confirmation as the second Level 3 action provider with atomic owner event publication.

description: Publish Sales order confirmation as the second genuine Level 3 action/event slice.

asi.hypothesis: Sales order confirmation already owns server-derived totals, authorization, idempotency, and invalid-state semantics, so atomic owner event publication and catalog metadata provide the smallest safe second Level 3 provider.

description: Strengthen Sales confirmation rollback proof through successful same-key recovery.

asi.hypothesis: A failed atomic Sales confirmation must leave status, confirmed timestamp, idempotency key, and outbox untouched, then permit a successful retry with the same key.
asi.rollback_reason: The PostgreSQL client's RowList metadata made a whole-array deepStrictEqual type-invalid even though the intended assertions were sound.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the proof using field-by-field assertions on rollbackRows[0], then confirm a same-key retry commits exactly one event.

description: Prove failed Sales confirmation is cleanly retriable with the same idempotency key.

asi.hypothesis: Field-level rollback assertions plus a successful same-key retry prove the atomic confirmation boundary is recoverable, not merely rolled back.
asi.rollback_reason: Behavior and all validation passed, but the new readiness gate searched for object-literal null assertions while the type-correct test used assert.isNull, so the primary metric did not improve.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the behavioral test and make the gate recognize the actual field-level assertions rather than requiring a specific assertion representation.

description: Prove Sales confirmation rollback clears all confirmation state and permits same-key recovery.

asi.hypothesis: A failed atomic Sales confirmation must leave status, confirmed timestamp, idempotency key, and outbox untouched, then permit a successful retry with the same key.

asi.validation: All nine readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Decouple Sales confirmation event identity from the Sales order aggregate identity.

asi.hypothesis: A domain event occurrence needs its own UUID rather than reusing the order aggregate ID, otherwise later Sales events for the same order would collide with the tenant-scoped outbox primary key.

asi.validation: All ten readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Give Inventory and Accounting owner events distinct occurrence identities.

asi.hypothesis: Inventory and Accounting event occurrences should not reuse correction or journal aggregate IDs, matching the envelope's distinct event identity and avoiding future same-aggregate event collisions.
asi.result: Both production and test services now generate independent event UUIDs while retaining correction/journal IDs as aggregate IDs and payload correlation; unit and PostgreSQL tests explicitly prove the identities differ.
asi.validation: All eleven readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Enforce UUID identity at all PUBLIC domain-event payload boundaries.

asi.hypothesis: PUBLIC event payload identifiers should validate as UUIDs, matching persisted domain identities and preventing malformed candidate events from entering catalog consumers.
asi.result: Inventory correction, Accounting revenue, and Sales confirmation payload schemas now validate their domain identifiers as UUIDs; compatibility fixtures use valid UUIDs.
asi.validation: All twelve readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Enforce owner namespaces for every typed domain-event declaration.

asi.result: Catalog compatibility now rejects event IDs that do not begin with the declared owning domain namespace across Inventory, Accounting, and Sales contributors.
asi.validation: All thirteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Bind every typed domain action identity to its authorization capability identity.

asi.hypothesis: A catalog action must authorize the capability with the same stable identifier; allowing action and capability IDs to diverge could protect a published business action with the wrong permission.
asi.result: Catalog compatibility now requires action.id to equal requiredCapability for both Inventory stock adjustment and Sales order confirmation providers.
asi.validation: All fourteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Validate typed event correlation and filter metadata as a coherent consumer contract.

asi.rollback_reason: The implementation was semantically valid but failed the repository formatter because the one-line for loop requires braces.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the assertions in formatter-compliant block form and rerun unchanged.

description: Validate typed event correlation and filter metadata as a coherent consumer contract.

asi.hypothesis: Event correlation fields must be nonempty, unique, and included in a duplicate-free filterable-field set so catalog consumers can reliably correlate and query candidates.
asi.result: Catalog compatibility now rejects empty or duplicate correlation metadata, duplicate filter metadata, and correlation fields that consumers cannot filter on.
asi.validation: All fifteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Validate every filterable event field against its declared payload schema.

asi.hypothesis: Catalog filter metadata must name real payload fields; otherwise consumers receive a published filter contract that cannot be evaluated against the event payload.

asi.validation: All sixteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove duplicate-safe consumer completion under concurrent PostgreSQL delivery.

asi.hypothesis: Sequential duplicate tests do not prove the receipt race; two concurrent deliveries must commit exactly one local effect and receipt while classifying the other as duplicate.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL consumeOnce proof now races two deliveries of the same event and verifies one winner, one duplicate, one derived event, and one durable receipt.
asi.validation: All seventeen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 117-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove the losing concurrent consumer rolls back a non-idempotent PostgreSQL-local mutation.

asi.hypothesis: The duplicate race must roll back a genuinely non-idempotent local mutation, because an idempotent derived-event append can mask a double execution defect.
asi.rollback_reason: The test imported the private messaging table, violating the repository rule that tests consume public contracts rather than persistence definitions.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the same transactional race using the public Database service with test-only SQL, without importing the private table schema.

description: Prove the losing concurrent consumer rolls back a non-idempotent PostgreSQL-local mutation.

asi.hypothesis: The duplicate race must roll back a genuinely non-idempotent local mutation, because an idempotent derived-event append can mask a double execution defect.
asi.result: Two concurrent consumeOnce calls now race an increment inside the ambient transaction; the proof verifies one winner, one duplicate, one committed increment, and one receipt without importing private messaging tables.
asi.validation: All eighteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 118-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove a failed consumer can recover with the same receipt identity.

asi.hypothesis: Receipt rollback is incomplete evidence unless the same consumer and event can subsequently retry, commit its local effect, and record one completed receipt.
asi.result: The failed-consumer PostgreSQL proof now retries the same receipt identity after rollback and verifies one recovered derived event and one completed receipt.
asi.validation: All nineteen readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 118-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove transaction-aware event append is idempotent under concurrent retries.

asi.hypothesis: Sequential append replay does not prove the outbox uniqueness race; concurrent identical envelopes must converge on one stored event and the same returned envelope.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof now races two identical append calls, verifies both return the same envelope, retains mismatch conflict behavior, and confirms one durable row.
asi.validation: All twenty readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 118-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove concurrent mismatched event envelopes fail with one typed conflict.

asi.hypothesis: Concurrent callers using the same event identity key with different envelopes must not both succeed; exactly one durable event and one typed idempotency conflict should result.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof now races mismatched envelopes sharing one event type, version, and idempotency key, verifying one success, one EventIdempotencyConflict, and one outbox row.
asi.validation: All twenty-one readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 119-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove messaging event and idempotency identities remain tenant-scoped.

asi.hypothesis: Tenant-scoped primary and deduplication keys must allow identical event IDs and idempotency keys in different tenants without cross-tenant conflict or envelope leakage.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof concurrently appends identical event, aggregate, and idempotency identities for two tenants, verifies distinct tenant envelopes, and confirms two durable rows.
asi.validation: All twenty-two readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 120-test portfolio passed.
asi.observation: Benchmark duration spiked to 527 seconds while correctness checks completed normally; no implementation change was made to optimize timing.

description: Prove cross-tenant consumer receipts fail without committing local effects.

asi.hypothesis: A consumer must not create a receipt for another tenant's event, and the foreign-key rejection must roll back any PostgreSQL-local effect attempted in the same transaction.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof uses a tenant-mismatched receipt around a non-idempotent increment, verifies a stable DatabaseFailure, and confirms zero increments and zero receipts.
asi.validation: All twenty-three readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 121-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove distinct consumers independently complete the same event.

asi.hypothesis: Receipt deduplication must be scoped by consumer as well as event and tenant; separate consumers should each commit their own local effect and durable receipt.
asi.result: Two distinct consumers concurrently process one event, both complete as non-duplicates, and the PostgreSQL proof verifies two committed increments and two receipts.
asi.validation: All twenty-four readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 122-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove concurrent event-ID collisions fail with one typed conflict.

asi.hypothesis: Within one tenant, an event ID must identify exactly one immutable envelope even when competing event types race; one append should win and the other return a stable idempotency conflict.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof races two different event envelopes sharing one tenant-scoped event ID, verifies one success, one EventIdempotencyConflict, and one durable row.
asi.validation: All twenty-five readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 123-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove event idempotency is scoped by event type and version.

asi.hypothesis: Because event identity is the type/version pair, the same tenant and idempotency key must permit distinct versions without false deduplication.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof concurrently appends versions 1 and 2 of the same event type with one idempotency key and verifies both independent durable envelopes.
asi.validation: All twenty-six readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 124-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove event idempotency is independently scoped by event type.

asi.hypothesis: Because event identity includes event type, the same tenant, version, and idempotency key must permit different event types without false deduplication.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof concurrently appends Sales and Inventory event types at version 1 with one idempotency key and verifies both independent durable envelopes.
asi.validation: All twenty-seven readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 125-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove messaging append joins and rolls back with an ambient transaction.

asi.hypothesis: A transaction-aware append must join its caller's active PostgreSQL transaction; a later caller failure must roll back an append that had already returned success.
asi.result: The PostgreSQL messaging proof appends inside Database.withTransaction, fails afterward, preserves the typed outer failure, and verifies no outbox row commits.
asi.validation: All twenty-eight readiness gates passed; full formatting, lint, type, skills, boundary, contract, and 126-test portfolio passed.

description: Prove invalid event envelopes fail at the messaging schema boundary.
